evidence: app/src/routes/abilities/[name].ts — the entire feature is one route file; deleting the directory removes the page
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:233 — the only inbound link to /abilities/ lives in the pokemon page's Abilities section, one block to delete
app/src/document.ts:26-30 — nav links are centralized here; no Abilities link exists, so nothing to scrub
app/src/routes/404.ts — unmatched URLs fall through to the catch-all automatically after removal
app/src/lib/data.ts:334 — getAbility (and ApiType-adjacent ApiAbility at :87) would be left dead in the data layer after route deletion
removability.rationale: Deleting the Abilities feature is a directory delete plus one section in the pokemon route — nearly the ideal case. The half-step down is that the data layer keeps dead helpers (getAbility/ApiAbility) that a careful remover must also grep for.

evidence: app/src/components/partials.ts:20-31 — cardLink is the single sprite render point for every card list (home, moves, abilities, types, team)
app/src/lib/api.ts:73-74 — spriteUrl derives the URL in one place
app/src/components/partials.ts:55 — cardList is the single place a sort could be added for all lists
app/src/lib/api.ts:5-9 — API base URL and cache TTL are defined in exactly one file

app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:168 — the isBuildRender guard is copy-pasted into all 7 route handlers (also (home).ts:18, moves/[name].ts:45, abilities/[name].ts:35, types/[name].ts:50, (types).ts:10, team.ts:89)
app/src/lib/data.ts:198 — card ids are produced in three places (cardsForPokemon :198, getPokemonIndex :236, routes/team.ts member :31), so a data-shape fix touches all three
changeability.rationale: Presentation-level bug fixes land in one obvious place (cardLink/spriteUrl/cardList/api.ts), which is the common case. Data-level fixes and any change to the build-render guard ripple across several files, which keeps this off the top score.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts — routes import narrow named functions (getMove, cardsForPokemon, getTypeLabels) rather than reaching into internals

app/src/lib/team.ts:3 — team state is one shared codec used by both server routes (routes/team.ts:91, routes/pokemon/[name].ts:170) and client store (client/team-store.ts:1), so server/client stay separated
app/src/document.ts:7-14 — the shell knows nothing about routes; CSS and client entry are wired in one place
app/src/client/pokemon-browser.ts:73 — island fetches the server template's '#results' by string selector, duplicated at routes/(home).ts:65; mismatch fails silently (fresh && current guard)
app/src/client/moves-panel.ts:24 — same stringly '#move-tables' contract with routes/pokemon/[name].ts:272
app/src/client/fragments.ts:4 — one module-level AbortController shared by all islands; two islands on one page would abort each other
coupling.rationale: Clean seams: routes depend on narrow lib exports, the server templates and client islands live in separate trees, and shared state flows through one module. The tangles are the untyped DOM-id contracts between islands and server templates, which break silently if renamed, and the global abort controller in fragments.ts.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts:198-213 — cardsForPokemon(items, ref, extra) is a genuinely generic helper reused by the move (:moves/[name].ts:19), ability (:abilities/[name].ts:18) and type (:types/[name].ts:52) routes
app/src/components/partials.ts:67 — count(n, noun) models the real Pokémon/moves variation without flags
app/src/components/partials.ts:20-52 — Card with optional types/hidden fields and cardLink/teamCard variants stretch to home, ability and team cases without duplication
app/src/lib/format.ts:5-15 — pure humanize/dexNumber/orDash helpers reused across all routes
app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:43-47 — load→null→404→title scaffolding is a fourth copy of the same pattern (also abilities :33, types :48, pokemon :166)
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:123 — the moveTables renderer plus its COLUMNS are embedded in (and exported from) the pokemon route rather than being a shared partial
abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions (Card, cardsForPokemon, section/count partials, format helpers) were designed around the app's real variation and stretch well — an Items section would reuse most of them. The gap is the repeated resource-route boilerplate and the moves-table renderer living inside a route file instead of components.

findings.issue: Islands couple to server templates via duplicated string selectors ('#results' at routes/(home).ts:65, '#move-tables' at routes/pokemon/[name].ts:272 vs client/moves-panel.ts:24, 'data-remove-member' at components/partials.ts:50 vs client/team-list.ts:12); a rename breaks the island silently because fetchFragment consumers no-op when the element is missing.
findings.suggestion: Put the shared element ids/attributes in one constants module imported by both the route template and the island, and log a warning in fetchFragment when the selector doesn't match.

findings.issue: The isBuildRender(url) guard is duplicated in all seven route handlers; a framework change to the build-stub hostname or a decision to prerender real data means seven edits.
findings.suggestion: Centralize it, e.g. a tiny withRouteData(load) wrapper each handler calls, or skip data loading in the shared api layer keyed off the same check.

findings.issue: A single module-level AbortController is shared by every island, so two fragment-fetching islands on one page would cancel each other's requests.
findings.suggestion: Create an AbortController per island (per custom element instance) and pass it to fetchFragment.

findings.issue: The load → null → responseInit.status = 404 → document title fallback pattern is copy-pasted across four resource routes, so a fix to 404 handling (e.g. also setting a header) lands in four places.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small resourceRoute(name, load, render) helper in components/ or lib/ and let each of the four routes delegate to it.

findings.issue: Card.id (used directly for the sprite URL) is produced in three places — cardsForPokemon (:198), getPokemonIndex (:236) and routes/team.ts member (:31) — and conflates species id with default-pokémon id; a sprite or id-semantics fix must keep all three in sync.
findings.suggestion: Have all three go through one card constructor (or at least one id-normalizing helper) so the species↔pokémon mapping has a single definition with a comment.

findings.issue: moveTables (plus its COLUMNS at :113) is exported from the route file but never imported anywhere; it's dead API surface in a route module.
findings.suggestion: Drop the export (or move the renderer into components/partials.ts where the other shared renderers live).

findings.issue: One 630-line global stylesheet holds every page's styles; well bannered by feature (Site chrome :47, Pokémon cards :173, Team :230, Home :293, Pokémon page :351, Move page :537, Types :549) so it's navigable, but removing a feature requires scanning for its section and there's no scoping guarantee.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is given the plain-CSS choice; if it grows, split per-route CSS files imported by the routes that use them.

summary: This is a well-factored codebase for its size: routes are thin, all cross-route logic lives behind narrow exports in lib/ and components/partials.ts, and the client islands reuse server templates via fragments instead of duplicating rendering. The recurring weaknesses are duplicated route-level boilerplate (the build-render guard and the 404 pattern) and stringly-typed DOM-id contracts between islands and templates that fail silently. Every requested change lands in one to three obvious places, which is what a maintainer actually experiences day to day.

It's not a 5 because card.id is computed in three producers (data.ts cardsForPokemon/getPokemonIndex, team.ts member) — if the fix is in the data rather than the URL, you must edit all three and keep them consistent.
